🔥🇲🇽 <u>Taxpayers Even Paid for Lorenzo Córdova's Wedding</u>

An internal electoral-institute document shows that on October 30, 2000, the IFE paid Lorenzo Córdova a "marriage dowry" of nearly 40,000 pesos in public money. The perk wasn't scrapped until 2017. The same Córdova whose INE turns up in the USAIDgate files.

🇲🇽⚖️ <u>Sheinbaum's Family-Justice Reform: Faster Adoptions, No More Hostage Divorces</u>

Sheinbaum sent Congress a reform of the National Code of Civil and Family Procedures. Between 25,000 and 35,000 children live in care centers, and 7 in 10 could be adopted if it weren't for red tape. The reform cuts the adoption suitability certificate from 90 to 45 days and lets judges check SAT and bank records so fathers can't hide income to dodge child support. It also orders protection within 24 hours against vicarious violence. "As if justice could be divided," said Arturo Zaldívar, "we are forcing children to live with their abusers."

🇲🇽🗳️ <u>INE Hands Its Stage to Somos "Experts" to Attack Morena's Majority</u>

In the middle of the electoral-materials contracts scandal, Mexico's INE hosted a forum on proportional representation and billed José Woldenberg, Jacqueline Peschard and Mariana Calderón as "independent specialists." Contralínea reports Woldenberg advises the right-wing party Somos and Calderón sits on its advisory council. Hours earlier, PAN's Ricardo Anaya had threatened to boycott the 2027 elections unless the plurinominal rules change. The "neutral experts" repeated the same script.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Salinas Pliego Calls for a Tax Revolt. Sheinbaum: He Owes Half the Country's Businessmen</u>

Mexico's tax-dodging billionaire Ricardo Salinas Pliego called for a "fiscal rebellion" against paying taxes. Sheinbaum's answer: "He owes money to half of Mexico's businesspeople… he owes in England, he owes in the United States." Paying taxes is the law, she reminded him, and collection is up 2% in real terms over 2025.

🇲🇽🏫 <u>Puebla Wipes Díaz Ordaz Off 29 Schools</u>

Puebla's education ministry stripped the name of Gustavo Díaz Ordaz — the president behind the Tlatelolco massacre of October 2, 1968 — from 29 public schools in 16 municipalities. They now carry the name "5 de Mayo," after the 1862 victory over the French invaders. Nationwide, 199 public schools still bear the name of the man who ordered troops to fire on students.

🇲🇽📊 <u>Banxico Raises Mexico's 2026 Growth Forecast to 1.9%</u>

Banxico lifted its 2026 GDP forecast from 1.5% to 1.9%, and it expects 2% in 2027 and 2.5% in 2028. The upgrade follows a pickup in activity in the second and third quarters. Governor Victoria Rodríguez Ceja said the economy still has slack, so the peso's recent swings should pass through to prices only in a limited way: "When demand is not strong, as is currently the case, that pass-through takes longer or is more limited."

🇲🇽🇪🇸 <u>Mexico and Spain: A New Era, Opened by a King's Admission</u>

Seven years after AMLO's letter asking Spain to apologize for the Conquest, which Madrid brushed off, Sheinbaum says relations are now "extraordinary." What changed was Felipe VI. At an exhibition of Mexican art in Madrid, the head of the Spanish state acknowledged that "atrocities" were committed during the Conquest. That gesture, Sheinbaum said, "opened a new stage in the relationship with both the Crown and the Government of Spain."

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Trump Says He Told Sheinbaum "Cartels Run Mexico." She Says It Never Came Up</u>

Back from Asia, Trump claimed that in Shenzhen he told Sheinbaum the cartels govern Mexico. Sheinbaum's answer: the 20-to-25-minute APEC meeting, with Ebrard and Velasco in the room, never touched the subject. "Maybe he was referring to another call, but in this meeting in China we spoke essentially about trade." When Trump has raised it on the phone, Mexico has answered the same way every time: the claim is false.
banner: TRUMP'S CARTEL CLAIM: 'IT NEVER CAME UP'

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Sheinbaum: Distrust in the INE Was Born in 2006 and 2012</u>

Sheinbaum traced the electoral institute's bad reputation to the 2006 fraud and the 2012 vote buying. A poll she presented found 58% call former INE chief Lorenzo Córdova corrupt (36% "very," 22% "somewhat"). Then she read a letter from the graphic-arts chamber, Canagraf: for years, middlemen with "no plant, no machinery and no workers" have cornered the contracts for electoral materials, shutting out an industry of more than 20,000 Mexican businesses.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Morena Goes After Private Insurers and Hospitals</u>

Ricardo Monreal presented a reform, signed by every bench coordinator, to rein in the medical-insurance business: portable policies that keep their seniority, agents forced to disclose their commissions, hospitals forced to publish price lists and hand over daily itemized bills, and seniors allowed to change deductibles without losing renewal rights. Thirteen million Mexicans have private coverage, and four companies collect 75% of all premiums. Last year the insurers' lobbyists killed a similar bill.
